faq: What does this tool calculate?
Arcminutes divided by 60, giving decimal degrees — with the precision you enter preserved through the conversion.
Is the calculation done locally?
Yes — in your browser, instantly. Nothing is sent anywhere to divide by sixty.
How accurate is the result?
Exactly as accurate as the input: the relation 60′ = 1° is definitional, so all error lives in the source value, none in the conversion.
Which datum do these coordinate tools use?
WGS84 — the GPS and web-map standard these pages share.
Do more decimal places always mean better accuracy?
No — they mean finer resolution. A coordinate measured to a metre gains nothing from eight decimals, a fact this site's precision tools quantify.
Can it convert a full coordinate?
This page converts the minutes component; paste whole coordinates into the Coordinate Converter or DMS to Decimal for the one-shot version.
Arcminutes versus minutes of time?
Different minutes entirely — 15 arcminutes of longitude pass per hour of Earth's rotation, which is the only bridge between them.
Negative values?
They convert with their sign — southern and western hemisphere arithmetic stays honest.
What about arcseconds?
One arcminute holds 60 arcseconds; the Arcseconds to Ground Distance Calculator gives those a physical size.
Why do charts still use minutes?
Because the nautical mile is built on them. At sea, minutes are not nostalgia — they are the unit system working as designed.
Rounding?
Results keep sensible precision; round deliberately with the Coordinate Rounding Tool when a form demands fewer places.
